Cyber Attack Disrupts Argentine Payments Network, Operations Restored

A cyber attack targeting Argentina’s national electronic payments network caused widespread disruption to business activity across the country last week, with energy producer Tecpetrol SA among the companies reporting operational impacts. The incident, which began late last Monday, paralyzed digital transactions and hampered payroll processing, supply chain payments, and retail activity nationwide until technical teams restored service on Thursday.

National infrastructure operator RedPagos Argentina confirmed the attack focused on its transaction processing systems. “Our cybersecurity protocols contained the breach, but service interruptions were unavoidable,” said RedPagos spokesperson Lucía Torres. She added that no customer funds were compromised, and all delayed payments are being cleared.

Tecpetrol SA, a major player in the energy sector, said the payments outage delayed deliveries and procurement processes. “Some of our operations were temporarily disrupted due to the inability to process vendor payments, but our facilities have resumed normal activity,” a Tecpetrol representative stated.

The Argentine Chamber of Commerce estimated that the three-day disruption affected over 120,000 businesses, especially in retail and logistics. “Electronic payments are the backbone of Argentina’s commerce. Even a short outage can translate into billions of pesos in lost transactions,” said analyst Sergio Mansilla of Buenos Aires-based consultancy Análisis Económico.

Authorities have not attributed the attack to any specific group but said a full investigation is underway. The National Directorate of Cybersecurity emphasized that new safeguards are being implemented. Labor unions welcomed the rapid restoration of services, but called for increased investment in digital infrastructure. “We need to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” said union leader Marta Benitez.
